title: Preventive Care Questions
about: The answers the chart doesn't hold that decide which USPSTF grade A and B screenings and preventive medicines a patient is due: tobacco history in pack-years, past cancers and bowel disease, cancers and other conditions in close relatives, sexual health in the past 6 months, where they were born and have lived, and pregnancy. Ask once, and again when something changes. The office section, written from the recommendations (USPSTF wording isn't reproduced), lists what each answer may point to; the clinician decides.

source.name: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, recommendations rated A and B

blocks.text: These questions help us know which tests and care may help you stay well. You can skip any question you would rather not answer.

blocks.text: For office use: what the answers may point to
Check each against the current USPSTF advice and the patient's age and history. The clinician decides.

items: Lung cancer scan: age 50 to 80, 20 or more pack-years, smokes now or quit in the last 15 years (Medicare: 50 to 77)
Aortic aneurysm scan, once: a man 65 to 75 who has ever smoked; Medicare also covers family history
BRCA risk tool: a woman with breast, ovarian, tube or peritoneal cancer in her or her family, or Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry
HIV PrEP: a partner with HIV, a recent STI, sex without condoms, shared needles, or asks for it
HIV, syphilis, chlamydia and gonorrhea tests: higher risk, or asks for a test
Hepatitis B test: born where it is common, parents from there, needles, men who have sex with men, or a contact with it
Hepatitis C test outside ages 18 to 79: ever injected drugs
TB test: born or lived where TB is common, or lived in a shelter, jail or prison
Bone density risk before 65 after menopause: a parent broke a hip, smoking, heavy drinking or low weight
Colon cancer screening from 45 is for average risk; past polyps, cancer, Crohn's or colitis need a different plan
Cervical screening stops after a hysterectomy that removed the cervix, with no past high-grade change
Folic acid 0.4 to 0.8 mg a day: could become pregnant, or plans to
